records.geographic_disambiguation: Kuk River as the downstream receiving-river identity for the selected connected system, including a southern headwater feeder and the separately named Avalik River approach. The selected object ends in a widened Kuk reach below the Avalik–Kaolak confluence, before the Ivisaruk junction.
records.completion_scope: Both original USGSTopo views were successfully acquired and visually inspected. Together with overlapping private reading crops they establish ordinary corridor correspondence for all 32 stored parts, the selected opening, tributary joins, Avalik–Kaolak confluence, Kuk wetland/widened reaches and actual stored terminal. The short generalized opening V does not select another drainage or require an undepicted intervening connection. The optional report pause does not leave a geographic gap.
records.supported_name_scope: Kuk labels directly support the downstream receiving reach; repeated Avalik labels support most of the selected upstream route. Distinct reach names coexist within the representative system identity. No scalar name is imposed on every feeder, nearby lake or individual reach.

scope_limits: The representative Kuk identity does not rename Avalik or its individual headwater feeders.
The chosen opening and short V are interpreted at ordinary feeder-corridor scale. Exact vertex coincidence, a formally named natural source and local current flow direction are not established.
The selected terminal lies in Kuk River; no extension to Wainwright Inlet or an open-sea mouth is inferred.
Map reading does not establish current water level, tidal stage, individual island-side channel, engineering operation or formal naming registry status.

records.region: Southern New Mexico and western Texas: Piñon Creek, Piñon Wash, Crow Flats and the Salt Basin east of Dell City.
records.material_pending_reason: Source material establishes named Piñon Creek, Piñon Wash and the actual Salt Basin terminal, but not the complete selected headward canyon connection, creek-to-wash transfer or long Crow Flats-to-playa continuation.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Piñon Creek names the upper/middle depicted river; Piñon Wash names a separate mapped downstream component. Salt Basin is the mapped terminal basin setting, not a proposed whole-system river name.
records.completion_scope: All 30 selected parts were considered. Piñon Creek, Piñon Wash and the actual Salt Basin terminal have bounded cartographic support. The selected Elk Canyon opening, creek-to-wash transfer and Crow Flats/inter-playa through-links remain materially incomplete.
records.supported_name_scope: Piñon Creek names the upper/middle depicted river; Piñon Wash names a separate mapped downstream component. Salt Basin is the mapped terminal basin setting, not a proposed whole-system river name.

scope_limits: The opening follows an identifiable canyon valley, but the acquired originals do not establish its full selected watercourse connection.
Intermittent channel depiction is accepted as ordinary correspondence. Dryness alone does not create any pending interval.
The source depicts the named creek and wash with an actual intervening unmapped link along the selection; shared hydronym roots do not close it.
The long Crow Flats plain and initial playa transfers remain unestablished; basin membership and sparse water symbols are not substituted for source correspondence.
The actual stored terminal is inside the mapped Texas Salt Basin playa, rather than the end of Piñon Creek or Piñon Wash.
A whole-system representative river name is not supported while material connections remain open. This is not a finding that local or official names do not exist.

records.region: Southern California, Los Angeles and Ventura counties
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative identity of the connected Aliso Canyon Creek–Santa Clara River coastal system. The upper component retains its own name; Santa Clara River is not assigned as a scalar name to every selected reach.
records.completion_scope: Completed ordinary corridor-scale correspondence of the one selected fragment and all 33 stored parts using a full-corridor original map, two targeted original details and explicit primary-source tributary relationships. Distinct upper naming and the estuarine terminal are preserved. No exact bank, vertex, current flow, operating regime or present sandbar opening is asserted.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity of the connected Aliso Canyon Creek–Santa Clara River coastal system. The upper component retains its own name; Santa Clara River is not assigned as a scalar name to every selected reach.

scope_limits: Composite topographic linework does not by itself depict an uninterrupted upper Aliso channel. The direct tributary inventory and matching valley geography provide the ordinary through-link; no present-flow or detailed hydraulic inference is made.
Upper-component name boundaries and exact headwater or tributary vertices are not fixed.
The final modeled endpoint is in the mapped estuarine mouth setting. Exact present shoreline and sandbar conditions are outside this naming assessment.
No mainstem lake or reservoir crossing is established or required by the selected route; nearby tributary reservoirs and recharge ponds are distinguished from it.
The representative candidate is not an accepted scalar label or a formal registry verification.

records.completion_scope: All 40 selected parts were considered. The mapped eastern Río de los Patos course, Aguas Calientes confluence and salar approach have bounded correspondence. The chosen southeastern opening, northern salar loop, southwestern return and actual western terminal remain incomplete.
records.supported_name_scope: Supported for the mapped river approach and downstream reach to the salar margin. scope_limits: The river name is a bounded reach finding, not an official registry determination or a verified whole-system scalar name.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
